text:
alex: ran the entropy-aware batch gating job on canary for the last 6h. wanted to share quick notes + numbers.

alex: config used: microbatch_interval=6ms, coalesce_delay=2ms, jitter=uniform(0,1.5ms), token_budget_target=48, queue_policy=priority-token.

meera: nice — what's the main motivation for the uniform jitter vs gaussian?

alex: main goal was to break up correlated arrivals from the web tier. uniform gave fewer coincident timers in our trace. gaussian created occasional 0.5–1ms clumps that hurt p99.

jia: fwiw I profiled the kernel selection path. when we increased token_budget_target from 32->48 we saw a kernel shift at ~120 tokens where the runtime chose the transformer-fused path instead of the matmul-tiling fallback. that changed per-token CPU usage. snippet from perf top: 

```
# hot stacks (summary)
transformer_fused_kernel    42%
matmul_tiled_kernel         26%
kv_cache_copy               12%
rpc_dispatch                8%
other                      12%
```

jia: implies we gain through better batching but pay in KV copy overhead for some sequences.

sam: any KV hit-rate numbers? curious if larger batches reduce cache locality.

alex: yes — canary saw KV hit-rate drop from 91% -> 86% during high conc bursts. overall token cost decreased ~6% but p95 tail rose 12ms. p50 improved 4ms.

meera: so tradeoff is cost vs tail. do we have per-route token_budget suggestions? e.g., short-completion routes vs long-running chat?

alex: proposal: route-level token_budget defaults: short_routes=24, interactive=48, long_jobs=128. use adaptive knob that decays budget if KV hit-rate < 80% for 2m.

perf-bot: Performance alert: canary cluster 3 reported p99 increase +18ms at 2026-03-17T11:22Z. Linked trace id: rwd-canary-218765.

jia: linked flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/r/218765 (short). shows long tail dominated by kv_cache_copy + kernel memcopy.

sam: idea: add a soft backpressure in queue_policy: when sample_queue_length>40 and kv_hit_rate<85% then reduce coalesce_delay by 33% and lower token_budget_target by 25% for 30s. this should favor latency at burst time.

meera: sounds reasonable. can we simulate? we should replay production arrival trace and run offline estimator to predict cost delta. alex can you run the trace with the soft backpressure rule?

alex: started a replay now — ETA ~45m. will capture p50/p95/p99, kv hit-rate, and model kernel selection histogram.

jia: also recommend adding a tiny prefetch window on KV hot keys for batches > 6 to amortize memcopies (proto: kv_prefetch=on, threshold=6). small probe showed memcopy per-batch reduced ~22%.

sam: if memcopy drops we might keep higher token budgets without tail regressions. nice. any correctness risk with prefetch?

jia: minimal — we only prefetch metadata + first 16KB of value, fallback to on-demand loads. safe for now.

alex: replay finished. summary: with soft backpressure enabled p99 dropped 9ms vs canary baseline, p50 similar, cost delta +1.2% on tokens, kv_hit-rate recovered to 89% during bursts. kernel histogram: fused_kernel share down 38% during bursts vs previous experiment.

meera: that looks promising — small cost bump for tail improvement. can we run a 24h canary with backpressure + kv_prefetch? then roll to 10% traffic.

sam: we should also add a metric: kernel_switch_rate (/s) and kv_memcopy_bytes/s so we can alert when kernel switching correlates with tail.

alex: noted. i'll add those to the canary dashboard panels and create an alert: kernel_switch_rate>10 for 1m -> warn.

perf-bot: CI: canary job rwd-canary-218765 completed. artifacts: logs + kernel_hist.json.

meera: plan then: (1) enable soft backpressure + kv_prefetch on canary for 24h, (2) monitor kernel_switch_rate & kv_memcopy_bytes, (3) if p99 stable -> 10% rollout with auto-revert if kernel_switch_rate spikes.

sam: +1. add runbook bullets for rollback thresholds (p99 +25ms or kernel_switch_rate x2).

alex: creating PR with config, dashboard, and runbook now. will tag you both. thanks :thumbsup:

meera: thanks team. quick note — document the uniform jitter choice in the config rationale. future: try poisson jitter to compare.

alex: added to PR description.

jia: 👍

sam: 👍

alex: closing thread after PR merged and canary live.
